Illustrative model. η = (σp − σv) / σx: how many times the slurry pressure in excess of the water pressure exceeds the earth pressure (η < 1: collapse, 1–1.3: small reserve). The earth pressure is calculated from the Schneebeli formula, layer by layer (γ above the GWT, γ′ below); the check is made below the guide wall (1.2 m). The real verification works with three-dimensional slip surfaces and safety factors, and in peat and very soft clay undrained behaviour and slurry loss are even more unfavourable.
Quiz – diaphragm walls
At least how far above the groundwater table should the slurry level in the trench be?
At least 5 m
It doesn’t matter if the slurry is dense enough
The slurry is only slightly heavier than water (1.03–1.12 g/cm³), so a head advantage is needed: at least 1.0–1.5 m. This excess also balances the earth pressure.
What is the typical length of a grab “bite”?
Why is the earth pressure on the wall of the trench smaller than the Rankine value?
Arching develops towards the two ends of the panel (silo effect)
The slurry chemically stabilises the soil
The buoyancy of the groundwater fully balances it
Because the diaphragm wall is flexible
Next to a trench of finite length, the soil wedge leans on the soil at rest at the ends of the panel; the earth pressure tends to a limit with depth (Schneebeli formula).
What happens if a longer panel is opened in the same soil?
Arching weakens, the earth pressure increases, and stability decreases
Stability increases
No effect, only concreting takes longer
The slurry density increases
Shorter panel → stronger arching → smaller earth pressure → more stable trench. That is why the panel length is at most 8–10 m, typically 2.8–5.6 m.
What kind of bentonite can be used for trenching?
Only activated “Na” bentonite
Any local clay
A mixture of quartz sand and water
Bentonite is a colloidal clay consisting predominantly of montmorillonite; only activated Na bentonite is suitable for trenching, and the viscosity can be increased with CMC.
At the latest, how long after the end of trenching must concreting start?
4–5 hours
24 hours
Only after the slurry has fully settled
As soon as possible, but no later than 4–5 hours afterwards – before that, base cleaning; then continuous, uninterrupted underwater concreting.
